card.title: Split So Each Letter Stays in One Part
card.sub: Two Pointers With Last Positions · Medium

a1.cap: Split the lowercase string s into as many parts as possible so every letter appears in at most one part. Return the sizes of the parts in order.

lines: Split the lowercase string s into as many parts as possible so every letter appears in at most one part. Return the sizes of the parts in order.

a1.cap: For example, with s = "ababcbacadefegdehijhklij", the answer is [9,7,8].
a1.say: For example, with s equals "ababcbacadefegdehijhklij", the answer is 9, 7, 8.

a1.cap: Record where each letter appears last. Grow the current part with a right pointer; the part must stretch at least to the last position of every letter it contains (end).
When right reaches end, close the part, record its size, and start the next part at left = right + 1.
a1.say: When right reaches end, close the part, record its size, and start the next part at left equals right plus 1.

a1.cap: Let's walk through it with s = "ababcbacadefegdehijhklij".
a1.say: Let's walk through it with s equals "ababcbacadefegdehijhklij".

a1.cap: Every letter in 'ababcbaca' ends here: a part of size 9.
Every letter in 'defegde' ends here: a part of size 7.
Every letter in 'hijhklij' ends here: a part of size 8.
Time complexity is O(n) and extra space is O(1).
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n and extra space is O of one.

a1.cap: That's the Two Pointers With Last Positions approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
